then he should sprinkle around with the seed "ram." Of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and Isha, and likewise of the world-guardians
and their weapons, having performed worship all around in order, the one who knows the rite, taking out fire to prepare incense, lamp and the rest,
and preparing again the materials beginning with ghee, arranging a seat in the fire and invoking there as before,
having worshipped the god and the Goddess, he should then perform everything up to the full oblation. Or the fire rite stated for his own order, offered to Shiva,
understanding it thus, one of Shiva's order may perform, and there is no other rule there. Ash from the Shiva fire should be collected, or that produced from the agnihotra,
or from the marriage fire, well burned, pure and fragrant. The dung of a tawny cow is commended, caught as it falls in the air,
not wet, not too hard, not foul-smelling, not dried out; if it has fallen, he should take it discarding the top and bottom.
Making it into balls, he should cast them into the Shiva fire and the like with the root mantra; discarding what is underburned or overburned, taking the white ash,
or stirring it well, he should put it into an ash vessel; of metal, wood, clay or stone,
or some other fine, clean ash vessel he should make; he should keep the ash like wealth in a level, auspicious, clean place.
a cubit is said by the good to be twenty-four fingers. There may be three girdles, or two, or one.

When setting out he should take the ash himself, or an attendant; he should not give it into an unfit hand nor throw it on an unclean floor, nor touch it with lower limbs, nor neglect it, nor step over it.
Therefore, taking the ash, he should apply it with mantras at the times stated and not otherwise, and not give it to the unfit.
He should collect the ash while the god has not yet been dismissed, since after the dismissal it becomes Chanda's ash.
After the fire rite is done, by the path taught in the Shiva shastra or in the manner stated in his own sutra, he should perform the bali rite.
Then, placing the seat of knowledge on a well-plastered mandala and installing the treasury of knowledge, he should worship it with flowers and the rest in order.
Making a mandala for the guru too in front of the knowledge, and setting an excellent seat there, he should worship the guru with flowers and the rest.
Then he should worship those worthy of honour and feed the hungry; then he himself should eat pure food at ease,
or what was offered to the god, its remnant, for self-purification, with faith and not from greed — but not what was offered to Chanda.
For fragrance, garlands and anything else the same rule applies; but the discerning man should not think there, "I am Shiva."
Having eaten and sipped water, meditating on Shiva, he should utter the root mantra in his heart, and spend the rest of the time with fitting talk on the Shiva shastras and the like.
he should make it as is beautiful, smooth, pleasing and firm with clay; the yoni like an ashvattha leaf, or like an elephant's lip,
When the first part of the night has passed, having performed a charming worship, he should arrange a single very splendid bed for Shiva and his consort,
and likewise foods, eatables, garments, unguents, flowers, garlands and the rest; having made everything charming, in mind or in deed,
then he should sleep pure at the feet of the god and the Goddess — a householder with his wife, and others alone.
Knowing the time of dawn, he should utter the first mantra, bowing in mind to the imperishable god with Amba and his hosts.
Having performed purification and the rest as befits place and time according to his ability, he should awaken the god and the Goddess with divine sounds of conches and the like.
Then, with very fragrant flowers blooming at that hour, completing the worship of Shiva and his consort, he should begin what was described before.
he should make it from the middle of the girdle, on the west or the south, beautiful, a little lower at the front, opening gently,
facing the fire-pit at its tip, leaving a little of the girdle. There is no rule of height for the altar; it may be of clay or of sand.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 28: the description of the rites for daily and occasional observance. Upamanyu said: Next I shall tell the order of occasional rites for those who live in Shiva's order, by the path taught in the Shiva shastra.
under the star called Shravishtha, then in Proshthapada, and he should sprinkle for the water sport on the day of Purvashadha;
in Ashvayuja he should then give sweet rice and new rice, and perform the fire rite with it on the day of Shatabhishaj;
in Kartika, in conjunction with Krittika, he should give a thousand lamps; in Margashirsha, under Ardra, he should bathe Shiva with ghee.
If unable at those times, he should hold a festival, or a court, or a great worship, or a more elaborate worship.
At the return of a festival, in auspicious rites, in dejection, bad conduct, bad dreams, ill sights,
portents or other misfortunes, or in severe illness, the rites of bathing, worship, japa, meditation, fire offering, giving and the like
should be performed according to the occasion, preceded by the preparatory rite. If the Shiva fire is interrupted, he should establish it again.
To one who thus abides devoted to Sharva's dharma, always diligent, Maheshvara grants liberation in a single birth.
Whoever performs these, each more than the last, in the daily and occasional rites goes to the first divine abode of lord Shrikantha.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there for a hundred crore kalpas, the man, falling from there in the course of time, reaches the world of Uma and of Kumara,
In all months, in both fortnights, on the eighth and fourteenth days and likewise on the parva days in order,
the world of Vishnu, of Brahma, and especially of Rudra; having dwelt there long and enjoyed the pleasures described,
and going higher again, passing beyond the five abodes, gaining knowledge from Shrikantha, he goes from there to Shiva's city.
One devoted to half the observance likewise returns twice; afterwards, gaining knowledge, he attains union with Shiva.
The embodied one who has observed a quarter, after the death of the body, passing beyond the two worlds up to the end of the cosmic egg or the unmanifest above,
reaching the Paurusha and Raudra abodes of the lord of the daughter of the king of mountains, enjoys pleasures in many ways for many thousands of ages;
when his merit is exhausted, reaching the earth he is born in a great family. There too, by the force of former impressions, that greatly radiant one,
abandoning the dharmas of the bound, becomes devoted to Shiva's dharma; by the weight of that dharma, meditating, he goes to Shiva's city.
Having enjoyed various pleasures, he goes to the state of the Vidyeshvaras; enjoying many pleasures there with the Vidyeshvaras in order,
he returns once more, within the cosmic egg or outside it; then gaining knowledge of Shiva and attaining supreme devotion,
attaining likeness in nature to Shiva, he does not return again. And one who is extremely devoted to Shiva, like one whose mind is attached to objects,
at the solstices and equinoxes, and especially at eclipses, a great worship, or a more elaborate one according to one's ability, should be performed.
is liberated whether he performs Shiva's dharmas or not. Returning once, twice or three times, he ceases to return;
one qualified for Shiva's dharma is not again bound to the wheel. Therefore, taking refuge in Shiva by whatever cause,
one should set one's mind on Shiva's dharma, if one strives for welfare. Here we shall compel no one by any means.
By nature this does not please those given to compulsion and extreme talk; it pleases others through the weight of meritorious impressions,
those in whom the cause of worldly existence is unable to sprout. Therefore, having considered this entirely according to one's nature,
one should take up Shiva's dharma, if one desires good for oneself.
Every month, having duly prepared the brahmakurcha and bathed Shiva with it, he should drink the remainder while fasting.
For faults like the killing of a brahmin, however great, no expiation surpasses the drinking of the brahmakurcha.
In Pausha, under the star Pushya, he should perform the waving of lights for the Lord; in Magha, under the star Magha, he should give a blanket of ghee.
In Phalguna, at the end of Uttara, he should begin a great festival; in Chaitra, on the full moon of Chitra, he should hold the swing festival according to rule.
In Vaishakha, under Vishakha, he should hold the great flower festival; in Jyeshtha, under the star Mula, he should have a cool pot given.
In Ashadha, under Uttarashadha, likewise the offering of the pavitra threads; in Shravana he should arrange even ordinary mandalas.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 29: the description of rites for particular desires. Shri Krishna said: Lord, I have heard from your own mouth, equal to the Shruti, the daily and occasional rites told by Shiva for those who take refuge in him.
The Maheshvaras are declared to be those on earth devoted to the sacrifice of action; therefore the Shaivas should perform it inwardly and the Maheshvaras outwardly.
But the procedure of the rite to be described does not differ. Having examined the ground according to rule by smell, colour, taste and the like,
in a place pleasing to the mind, under a canopy spread wide, on a well-plastered piece of ground like the inside of a mirror,
he should first determine the east by the path seen in the shastra, and prepare a mandala of one cubit or two.
He should draw a spotless eight-petalled lotus with its pericarp, with powders of jewels, gold and the like, gathered as available,
with the five enclosures, rich in decoration. On the petals the powers are to be arranged, and on the filaments, with their Shaktis,
the eight Rudras beginning with Vama, from the eastern petal in order; on the pericarp dispassion, and on the seeds the nine Shaktis;
on the bulb dharma of the nature of Shiva, on the stalk knowledge resting in Shiva; above the pericarp the orbs of fire, sun and moon;
after that the three principles called Shiva, Vidya and Atma; above all the seats, a comfortable one strewn with many-coloured flowers.
He should worship with the five enclosures, together with Amba, him who is like pure crystal, gracious, of cool radiance,
Now I wish to hear, if there are also rites for particular desires for those qualified for Shiva's dharma; please tell them now.
adorned with a crown of matted locks like rings of lightning, clad in a tiger-skin, his lotus face slightly smiling,
the soles of his feet and hands and his lips like petals of a red lotus, endowed with every mark, adorned with every ornament,
bearing excellent divine weapons, anointed with divine fragrance, five-faced, ten-armed, with a crescent moon as crest-jewel.
His eastern face is gentle, radiant like the morning sun, rich with three lotus eyes, crowned with the young moon;
the southern, lovely in lustre like a dark blue cloud, fierce with knitted brows, with three round red eyes,
dreadful with fangs, unassailable, with quivering lips; the northern like coral, adorned with dark locks,
playful, three-eyed, crowned with the moon as ornament; the western like the full moon, bright with three eyes,
bearing the crescent, gentle, charming with a soft smile; the fifth like crystal, bright with the crescent of the moon,
exceedingly gentle, shining with three wide-open eyes; on the right shining with trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire,
and on the left shining with serpent, arrow, bell, noose and goad; bound up to the knees by Nivritti, up to the navel by Pratishtha,
Upamanyu said: There is some with a fruit in this world, some with a fruit in the next, and some with both; and it is again fivefold.
up to the throat by Vidya, likewise up to the forehead by Shanta, and above that by the supreme kala called Shantyatita;
pervading the five paths, his very body the five kalas; the god crowned by Ishana, the ancient one called Purusha,
with Aghora as his heart, likewise Vama as his private parts, Maheshvara, with Sadya as his feet, his form made of the thirty-eight kalas,
Ishana made of the letters, made of the five Brahmans, made of what is called Omkara, joined with the Shakti of the hamsa,
with the Shakti of the nature of will seated on his lap, with the one called Knowledge on the right and the one called Action on the left,
made of the three principles, Sadashiva, the very form of knowledge. Having conceived the form with the root mantra and made it whole in order,
and worshipped it as is right up to the arghya with the root knowledge, Shiva embodied, in person, together with the supreme Shakti,
invoking there Mahadeva, free of manifestation as being or non-being, and making the five services, he should worship the supreme Lord,
with the Brahman mantras and the six limbs, then with the letters, with the pranava, with Shiva's mantra joined with Shakti in order,
or with the peaceful mantra and other Vedic mantras in full; he should worship the supreme god, or with Shiva's mantra alone.
Some rites consist of ritual action, some of austerity,
Having performed everything from water for the feet to mouth-freshener, without the dismissal, he should begin the worship of the five enclosures in order.
some of japa and meditation, and some of all; that consisting of ritual action is divided by the order of fire offering, giving and worship.
It is fruitful only for those who possess all power, not for others; and power is the command of Mahesha, Shiva, the supreme self.
Therefore a twice-born who bears his command should perform rites for desires. Now I shall tell of the rite for desires that gives fruit here and hereafter.
It should be performed by Shaivas and Maheshvaras, inwardly and outwardly respectively. Shiva and Maheshvara are not really different here;
just so, Shaivas and Maheshvaras too are not different. The Shaivas are men who take refuge in Shiva, devoted to the sacrifice of knowledge.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 30: the description of the rites for desires of the Shaivas. There, first, on the right and left sides of Shiva and his consort in order, he should worship with fragrance and the rest the two gods Heramba and Shanmukha.
In the second enclosure the Chakravartins of all the seasons are to be worshipped; in the third enclosure the eight forms with their Shaktis:
Therefore there is no greater protection for oneself here than this; knowing this and performing this rite, one attains good.
Whoever, being pure and well collected, recites only the hymn obtains an eighth part of the fruit of his most desired aim.
One who, contemplating its meaning, recites it fasting on a parva day, or on the eighth or fourteenth, obtains half the fruit.
But one who, contemplating its meaning and keeping the vow on the parva days and the like, recites the hymn for a month obtains the whole fruit.
in the eight directions in order, from the east all around: Bhava, Sharva, Ishana, Rudra, then Pashupati,
Ugra, Bhima and Mahadeva — the eight forms in order. Then after that, Mahadeva and the others in order, the eleven forms, are to be worshipped there with their Shaktis:
Mahadeva, Shiva, Rudra, Shankara, Nilalohita, Ishana, Vijaya, Bhima, Devadeva, Bhavodbhava
and Kapardisha are named, with eleven Shaktis likewise. Of these, eight are to be worshipped first, from the south-east in order;
Devadeva on the eastern petal and Ishana in the south-east, Bhavodbhava between them, and Kapalisha after that.
In that enclosure again he should worship the king of bulls in front, Nandi to its right and Mahakala to the north,
Shasta on the south-eastern petal, the Mothers on the southern petal, the elephant-faced on the south-western, Shanmukha on the western,
Jyeshtha on the north-western petal, Gauri on the northern, Chanda on the north-eastern; between Shasta and Nandisha he should worship the lord of sages, Vrishabha;
to the north of Mahakala he should worship Pingala; between Shasta and the host of Mothers, then Bhringishvara;
Then the Brahmans around, from Ishana to Sadya in order, with their Shaktis, he should worship in the first enclosure,
between the Mothers and Vighnesha he should worship Virabhadra; between Skanda and Vighnesha he should worship the goddess Sarasvati;
between Jyeshtha and Kumara, Shri, who worships Shiva's feet; between Jyeshtha and Ganamba he should worship Mahamoti;
between Ganamba and Chanda he should worship the goddess Durga. In this same enclosure again, the host of Shiva's attendants,
the various ones called Rudras, Pramathas and Bhutas, with their Shaktis, and the group of Shiva's consort's friends, he should worship, meditating with collected mind.
When the third enclosure has thus been fully worshipped, meditating on the fourth enclosure outside it, he should worship.
The Sun is to be worshipped on the eastern petal, the four-faced on the southern, Rudra on the western petal and Vishnu on the northern.
Then the separate enclosures of the four gods: first its six limbs with the Shaktis beginning with Dipta:
Dipta, Sukshma, Jaya, Bhadra, Vibhuti, Vimala in order, Amogha and Vidyuta, placed all around from the east.
In the second enclosure the four forms are to be worshipped in order, from the east to the north, and after them the Shaktis:
Aditya, Bhaskara, Bhanu and Ravi in succession; Arka, Brahma, Rudra and Vishnu — these belong to Vivasvat;
and the six limbs there too, from the heart onward in order, of Shiva and of Shiva's consort, he should worship from the south-east.
Vistara in the eastern part, Sutara in the south, Bodhani in the western part and Apyayini in the north.
Usha, Prabha, Prajna and then Sandhya, placing them from the north-east onward, he should worship in the second enclosure.
Soma, Angaraka, Budha the best of the wise, Brihaspati of great intellect, Bhargava the treasury of radiance,
Shanaishchara, Rahu and dreadful smoky Ketu — these he should worship all around in the third enclosure in order.
Or he may worship the twelve Adityas in the second enclosure and the twelve signs of the zodiac in the third.
And outside it, all around, the seven groups of seven: sages, gods, gandharvas, serpents, hosts of apsarases,
gramanis, yakshas, yatudhanas, the horses made of the seven metres, and the Valakhilyas he should worship.
Having thus worshipped the sun in the third enclosure, he should then worship Brahma with three enclosures.
He should worship Hiranyagarbha in the east, Viraj in the south, Kala in the western part and Purusha in the north.
Hiranyagarbha, the first Brahma, is like a lotus; Kala is like jati collyrium; Purusha is like crystal;
There, afterwards, he may or may not worship the eight Rudras beginning with Vama with the Shaktis beginning with Vama, all around from the east in order.
the three-qualitied, the rajasic, the tamasic and the sattvic — these four stand in order in the first enclosure.
In the second enclosure are to be worshipped, all around from the east in order, Sanatkumara, Sanaka, Sananda and Sanatana.
Afterwards in the third enclosure he should worship the Prajapatis, eight in the east and the rest, three east and west in order:
Daksha, Ruchi, Bhrigu, Marichi, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri, Kashyapa
and Vasishtha — these are renowned as the lords of creatures. Their wives too are to be worshipped with them in order:
Prasuti, Akuti, Khyati, Sambhuti, Dhriti, Smriti, Kshama, Sannati, Anasuya,
the mother of the gods and Arundhati — all chaste wives, ever devoted to the worship of Shiva, glorious and lovely to behold.
In the first enclosure he may worship the four Vedas; in the second, the Itihasas and Puranas;
afterwards, in the third enclosure, all the Vedic sciences headed by the Dharmashastras are to be worshipped all around.
The Vedas in front from the east, the others as he likes, arranging the worship around in eight or four parts.
The first enclosure has been told to you by me, son of Yadu's line; the second enclosure is told with love — hear it with faith.
Having thus worshipped Brahma with his three enclosures, he should then worship Rudra with his enclosures in the south-west.
His Brahman mantras and six limbs are remembered as the first enclosure, and the second enclosure likewise is made of the Vidyeshvaras.
In the third enclosure there is a difference, which is now told: his four forms are to be worshipped from the east in order.
The three-qualitied, with parts, the god called Shiva, in front; the rajasic, Brahma the creator, worshipped as Bhava, in the south;
the tamasic, Agni, to be worshipped in the west as Hara the destroyer; the sattvic, giver of happiness, in the north, Vishnu the lord of the universe, Mrida.
Having thus worshipped in the western part Shambhu's Shiva of the twenty-six principles, he should then worship Vaikuntha on the northern side.
Placing Vasudeva in front, he should worship in the first enclosure Aniruddha in the south, then Pradyumna in the west,
and Sankarshana in the north, or he may worship these two interchanged. The first enclosure has been told; the auspicious second enclosure:
the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-Lion, then the Dwarf, one of the Ramas, Krishna, and the Horse-faced one.
In the third enclosure he should worship the discus in the eastern part; in the south he should worship the weapon called Narayana, unobstructed anywhere;
He should worship Ananta on the eastern petal and his Shakti to his left, Sukshma on the southern petal together with his Shakti,
in the west the Panchajanya, and in the north the bow Sharnga. Thus with three enclosures, the supreme Hari himself, called Vishva,
making him embodied as Mahavishnu or Sadavishnu, he should worship. Having thus worshipped the four forms in the order of Vishnu's fourfold arrangement, he should worship their four Shaktis in order:
Prabha in the south-eastern part, Sarasvati in the south-west, Ganambika in the north-west and Lakshmi in the north-east.
Having thus performed the worship of the forms beginning with the Sun and of their Shaktis, he should worship the world-guardians in that same enclosure:
Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirriti, Varuna, Vayu, Soma, Kubera, and afterwards Ishana.
Having thus worshipped the fourth enclosure according to rule, he should then worship the weapons of Mahesha outside.
The glorious trident in the north-east, the thunderbolt in the direction of the great Indra, the axe in the direction of fire, and in the south he should worship the arrow;
in the south-west he should worship the sword, the noose in the domain of Varuna, the goad in the north-west and the Pinaka in the north.
He should worship the fierce Kshetrapala facing west. Having worshipped the fifth enclosure, then outside,
outside the deities of all the enclosures or in the fifth, in the fifth he should worship the great bull in front together with the Mothers.
then on the western petal Shivottama with his Shakti, and likewise on the northern petal he should worship Ekanetra;
then Ekarudra and his Shakti he should worship on the north-eastern petal, and Trimurti and his Shakti on the south-eastern petal;
Then all the classes of divine beings are to be worshipped all around: sky-goers, sages, siddhas, daityas, yakshas and rakshasas,
the lords of serpents headed by Ananta with the nagas born of their families, dakinis, bhutas, vetalas, pretas and the leaders of the Bhairavas,
and others dwelling in the netherworlds, born of various wombs; rivers, oceans, mountains, forests and lakes,
beasts, birds, trees, insects and other small creatures, men of various forms, and deer and other small creatures,
the worlds within the cosmic egg, then the crores of cosmic eggs, the countless worlds outside the egg with their rulers,
the Rudras who uphold the cosmic egg, stationed in the ten directions; whatever is of the qualities, of maya, or of Shakti beyond that,
whatever exists that can be denoted by a word, conscious or unconscious — all that, understood as beside Shiva and his consort, he should worship in general.
All with folded hands, inconceivable, with smiling faces, ever gazing lovingly at the god and the Goddess.
Having thus performed the worship of the enclosures, to calm distraction he should worship the lord of gods again and utter the five syllables.
Then he should offer to Shiva and his consort a pure, lovely great charu like nectar, with fine relishes,
the best made with thirty-two adhakas, the least with no less than one adhaka; having prepared it according to his means, he should offer it with faith.
Then, offering drinking water and betel with condiments, and performing the waving of lights and the rest, he should complete the rest of the worship.
He should prepare only excellent materials fit for enjoyment; a devotee who has the means should not be niggardly with wealth.
For the deceitful, the negligent and one who performs it defectively, rites for desires do not bear fruit — so say the good.
Therefore, giving up negligence completely and joining all the limbs, one should perform rites for desires if one wishes the fruit to be attained.
Having thus completed the worship and bowed to the god and the Goddess, fixing his mind in devotion, he should then utter the hymn.
Then, having worshipped with the hymn, at the end he should eagerly recite the five-syllabled knowledge no less than a hundred and eight times, or more than a thousand.
Having performed the worship of the knowledge and of the guru in order, he should honour the members of the assembly too according to his means and faith.
Then, dismissing the lord of gods with all the enclosures, he should give the mandala to the guru together with the implements of worship,
or give everything in order to those who take refuge in Shiva, or offer it to Shiva himself in a holy place of Shiva.
Shrikantha on the south-western petal and his Shakti to his left, and likewise on the north-western petal he should worship Shikhandisha;
Or he may worship the god in the Shiva fire with the seven materials of offering, having duly worshipped all the deities of the enclosures.
This is called Yogeshvara, renowned in the three worlds; there is no sacrifice anywhere in the world greater than it.
There is nothing in this world that cannot be accomplished by it, whether a fruit in this world or in the next.
It is not restricted by saying "this is its fruit, not that"; it is the best means to the whole of what is good.
What a man obtains by worshipping with it cannot be told; from it, as from a wish-granting gem, he obtains the fruit he seeks.
Even so, one should not use it aiming at a petty fruit, since one who seeks the small from the great becomes himself smaller.
Whether the fruit is great or small, if the rite is performed it succeeds; let the rite be performed with Mahadeva in view.
Therefore for fruits seen and unseen that cannot be gained otherwise, such as victory over enemies and death, the discerning should perform it.
In great sins too, in fear of great disease and the like, in famine and the like, one should perform a rite of pacification with it for peace.
What need of much talk? Maheshvara has declared this the Shaivas' own weapon, the remover of great calamities.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 31: the description of the great hymn to Shiva. Upamanyu said: I shall tell you, Krishna, the hymn by the path of the five enclosures, by which this holy Yogeshvara rite is completed.
Salutation to the supreme god, salutation to the supreme cause; salutation to you, Shiva, the peaceful; salutation to you, more auspicious still.
of uncommon deeds in the order of creation, preservation and dissolution; thus divided threefold, fourfold, and again fivefold,
worshipped in Shambhu's fourth enclosure together with his followers, dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, delighting in the worship of Shiva's feet —
honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he bestow blessing on me. The six limbs of the sun and the eight Shaktis beginning with Dipta,
Aditya, Bhaskara, Bhanu and Ravi in succession, Arka, Brahma, Rudra and Vishnu — the forms of the sun;
Vistara, Sutara, Bodhini and Apyayini, and others: Usha, Prabha, Prajna and Sandhya — these Shaktis too;
the planets from Soma to Ketu, devoted to Shiva, impelled by the command of Shiva and his consort, may they bestow blessing on me.
Or the twelve Adityas and likewise the twelve Shaktis, the sages, gods, gandharvas, and the hosts of serpents and apsarases,
the gramanis, yakshas, rakshasas and gods likewise — these seven groups of seven, the horses made of the seven metres,
and the Valakhilyas and the rest, all worshippers of Shiva's feet — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they bestow blessing on me.
Now Brahma, a form of the god of gods, ruler of the earth's sphere, possessing the lordship of sixty-four qualities, established in the principle of intellect,
This whole world with gods and asuras is dependent on you;
beyond qualities, mixed with qualities, and likewise qualities alone, the god of changeless nature, then common before,
of uncommon deeds in the order of creation, preservation and dissolution; thus divided threefold, fourfold, and again fivefold,
worshipped in Shambhu's fourth enclosure with his followers, dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, delighting in the worship of Shiva's feet —
honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he bestow blessing on me. Hiranyagarbha, lord of the world, Viraj, Kala and Purusha,
Sanatkumara, Sanaka, Sananda and Sanatana, and the lords of creatures, Daksha and the others, sons of Brahma,
the eleven with their wives, Dharma and Sankalpa — these delighting in the worship of Shiva, devoted to Shiva,
all under the sway of Shiva's command, may they bestow blessing on me. And the four Vedas with the Itihasas and Puranas,
the Dharmashastras with the Vedic sciences, of mutually consistent meaning, setting forth Shiva's nature —
honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they bestow blessing on me. Now Rudra, Mahadeva, the weightiest form of Shambhu,

father and also son of Vishnu, and his controller, the lord who always enlightens both and shows them grace,
Rudra dwelling within and without the cosmic egg, lord of the two worlds, dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, delighting in the worship of Shiva's feet —
placing Shiva's command foremost, may he bestow blessing on me. His Brahman mantras and six limbs, and likewise the eight Vidyeshas,
and the four divisions of his form headed by Shiva, worshippers of Shiva — Shiva, Bhava, Hara and Mrida — placing Shiva's command foremost, may they bestow blessing on me.
Now Vishnu, the supreme body of Mahesha, Shiva himself, ruler of the principle of water, abiding directly in the state of the unmanifest,
beyond qualities, abounding in sattva, and likewise qualities alone, identifying with changelessness, of change common to the three,
of uncommon deeds, apart from causing creation and the rest, vying even with the self-born one who arose from the right side,
created directly by the first Brahma and also his creator; Vishnu dwelling within and without the cosmic egg, lord of the two worlds,
And this person has you as his only refuge always; therefore, showing him grace, grant what he prays for.
destroyer of asuras, the discus-bearer, and younger brother of Shakra too, who appeared here tenfold under pretext of Bhrigu's curse,
who descended to earth by his own will to relieve the earth's burden, of immeasurable strength, the master of maya, deluding the world by maya,
worshipped daily by Vaishnavas on the seat made of the three forms, as Mahavishnu or Sadavishnu embodied,
dear to Shiva, attached to Shiva, delighting in the worship of Shiva's feet — placing Shiva's command foremost, may he bestow blessing on me.
Vasudeva, Aniruddha, then Pradyumna, and Sankarshana — these are declared the four forms of Hari;
the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-Lion, then the Dwarf, the three Ramas, Krishna, and Vishnu the horse-faced;
the discus, Narayana's weapon, the Panchajanya and the Sharnga — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they bestow blessing on me.
Prabha, Sarasvati, Gauri and Lakshmi, devoted to Shiva — by the command of Shiva and his consort may they bestow blessing on me.
Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirriti, Varuna, Vayu, Soma, Kubera and Ishana the trident-bearer,
all delighting in the worship of Shiva, devoted to Shiva's true being — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they bestow blessing on me.
Victory, Ambika, Mother of the world; victory, you who are made of the whole world; victory, you of unsurpassed lordship; victory, you of incomparable form.
The trident, the thunderbolt, the axe and the arrow, the sword, the noose, the goad and the Pinaka, the best of weapons —
these divine weapons of the god and the Goddess, honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may they always protect me.
The god in the form of a bull, son of Surabhi, of great strength, rivalling the submarine fire, surrounded by the five cow-mothers,
who attained the role of vehicle of the supreme couple by austerity — placing their command foremost, may he grant my desire.
Nanda, Sunanda, Surabhi, Sushila and Sumanas — these five cow-mothers dwell in Shiva's world,
ever devoted to Shiva, intent on the worship of Shiva; by the command of Shiva and his consort alone may they grant what I desire.
Kshetrapala of great radiance, like a dark blue cloud, his face dreadful with fangs, shining with quivering red lips,
with red hair standing up, glorious, his eyes crooked with knitted brows, with three round red eyes, adorned with the moon and serpents,
naked, his hands raised with trident, noose, sword and skull, Bhairava surrounded by Bhairavas, siddhas and yoginis,
seated in every holy field, standing as protector of the good, supremely devoted to bowing to Shiva, devoted to Shiva's true being,
Victory, you who are beyond speech and mind; victory, destroyer of the darkness of the insentient; victory, you who are free of birth and old age; victory, you who are higher than time.
protecting especially those who take refuge in Shiva as his own sons — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may he bestow blessing on me.
Talajangha and the rest, worshipped in his first enclosure — honouring the command of Shiva and his consort, may those four protect me.
Bhairava and the others who surround him on all sides — may they too favour me out of reverence for Shiva's command.
Narada and the other divine sages worshipped by the gods, the Sadhyas, the nagas and the gods who dwell in the Jana world,
those whose office has ceased, dwelling in the Mahar world, the seven sages and others together with the hosts of those in celestial chariots —
all delighting in the worship of Shiva, under the sway of Shiva's command — by the command of Shiva and his consort may they grant me what I desire.
The four classes of divine beings from gandharvas to pishachas, the siddhas, vidyadharas and others who move in the sky,
the asuras and rakshasas dwelling in the netherworlds, the lords of serpents headed by Ananta, the birds headed by Vainateya,
the kushmandas, pretas, vetalas, grahas and other hosts of bhutas, dakinis, yoginis and shakinis of the same kind,
fields, gardens, houses and the like, holy places and shrines, islands, oceans, rivers, streams and lakes,
Victory, you who abide in many forms; victory, beloved of the lord of the universe; victory, you who are worshipped by all the gods; victory, you who unfold the universe.
the mountains headed by Sumeru, the forests all around, beasts, birds, trees, worms, insects and the like, and deer,
all the worlds and the rulers of the worlds, the cosmic eggs with their enclosures, the directions and the ten elephants of the quarters,
letters, words and mantras, the principles with their rulers, the Rudras who uphold the cosmic egg, and other Rudras with their Shaktis,
and whatever in this world is seen, inferred or heard — may all grant my desire by the command of Shiva and his consort alone.
Now the supreme Shaiva knowledge, which frees the bound from the noose, called the Panchartha, divine, excluded from the knowledge of the bound,
and the shastra called Shivadharma and the one called Dharma after it, the Purana called Shaiva and Shivadharma, equal to the Shruti,
and the other Shaiva Agamas, the Kamika and the rest of four kinds, honoured and worshipped here without distinction from Shiva and his consort,
commanded by those two alone for the accomplishment of my aim — may they approve this rite as fruitful and well performed.
The teachers from Shveta to Nakulisha with their disciples, and the gurus of their lineage, and especially my own gurus,
the Shaivas and Maheshvaras devoted to knowledge and rite — may they approve this rite as fruitful and well performed.
Victory, you of auspicious divine limbs; victory, lamp of auspiciousness; victory, you of auspicious conduct; victory, giver of auspiciousness.
All worldly brahmins, kshatriyas and vaishyas in order, knowing the truth of the Vedas and Vedangas, skilled in all the shastras,
the men of Sankhya, Vaisheshika, Yoga and Nyaya, the Sauras, Brahmas, Raudras and other Vaishnava men,
all the cultured and the eminent, bound by Shiva's command — may they approve this rite that accomplishes my aim.
